name: WSMR

profile.address: 120, Aberdeen Avenue, Technical Area, White Sands Missile Range, White Sands, Doña Ana County, New Mexico, 88002
profile.reading:
The Information Systems Facility at White Sands Missile Range is a purpose built military communications and data processing building on the Army's largest fully instrumented open air test range, located in the range's Technical Area in Dona Ana County, New Mexico. The U.S. Army broke ground on the facility on August 24, 2021, describing it at the time as the first major military construction project undertaken at White Sands Missile Range in nearly two decades. The building was designed as a two story, 56,268 square foot structure intended to replace a telephone and administrative network core building dating back to 1962, consolidating networking, communications, data processing, Land Mobile Radio control, and general IT support functions that had previously been scattered across several older buildings on the installation.

Army officials put the total project cost at approximately 70.6 million dollars, split roughly between about 53 million dollars for construction and 17.6 million dollars for equipment, and construction was projected for completion in December 2023. The scope reflects the facility's role as critical infrastructure for range operations rather than a leasable commercial building. White Sands Missile Range runs extensive missile, rocket, and weapons testing across more than 3,200 square miles of restricted airspace and land, and that mission depends on reliable, centralized command, control, and communications systems, exactly the kind of consolidated networking and data processing core this building was built to house.

As is standard for facilities on an active military installation, White Sands Missile Range and the Army have not published detailed technical specifications for the completed building beyond what was disclosed at groundbreaking, such as its critical IT power capacity, its server or rack density, or its cooling architecture. There is no commercial tenant list because the building serves the range's own military and testing mission rather than outside customers, and no third party colocation or capacity data exists for it the way a commercial provider's facility would. That absence of public technical detail is expected and unremarkable for a facility supporting an active Army test range, and it reflects routine operational security rather than anything unusual about the project.

reading.body:
White Sands Missile Range built a new consolidated communications and data processing facility to replace a 1962 building, at a cost of approximately 70.6 million dollars, but published no power capacity or technical specifications for it.

Military installations require data processing infrastructure the same way commercial operators do, but the public record for this facility exists only as Army construction announcements rather than capacity spec sheets. The Information Systems Facility, completed as planned in December 2023 according to the project timeline, consolidates networking, communications, data processing, Land Mobile Radio control, and IT support functions that had previously occupied four separate buildings. At 56,268 square feet across two stories, it serves the range's command and control mission for weapons testing across more than 3,200 square miles of restricted airspace.

The absence of published power capacity, cooling specifications, or rack density is routine for active military installations and reflects operational security rather than incomplete data. This registry records the facility with capacity unspecified because no critical IT megawatt figure exists in the public domain. Readers assessing government infrastructure contributions to national compute capacity should note that military data centers operate outside commercial reporting systems and therefore do not appear in conventional capacity surveys, despite their material role in government operations and testing missions.
